headline: Maye shows serious grit as Patriots ground the Jets at home
morning_brew: That win over the Jets was exactly the kind of physical, ugly football you expect when these two meet up at Gillette. We controlled the clock, leaned on the ground game, and let the defense do the heavy lifting to move us to a winning record. Drake Maye looked composed under pressure, hitting his targets when we needed to move the chains, and that fourth quarter drive to put the game on ice was a thing of beauty. I haven't seen a clock-killing drive that satisfying since the glory days. Satisfied is the only way to feel after taking down a division rival, especially with the way the guys battled back in that second half.

My pops always said a win is a win, even if it doesn't win you any style points, and he would have loved the way we wore them down in the trenches. DeMario Douglas was all over the field, making plays and finding soft spots in the coverage that kept the chains moving all afternoon. It wasn't perfect, and that third quarter gave me a few gray hairs—I was watching through my fingers like it was a horror flick—but seeing this squad hold firm when the pressure was cranked up is a massive step forward for a group finding its identity.

Now we have to turn the page and get ready for a short week, with a trip out to Chicago to face the Bears on Thursday. There isn't much time to celebrate after a divisional battle like that, and the coaches know we need to clean up those lapses before heading into a hostile stadium. I'll be spending the next few days hoping for a clean injury report and keeping my fingers crossed that the momentum we built at home carries over to the road.
